discoveries.title: Passenger compensation management
discoveries.discovery: TOCs manage passenger compensation during delays and incidents, but it represents a broader operational subsystem that could be linked.
discoveries.source_basis: Mentioned during delay management and operational incidents where TOCs handle passenger compensation.
discoveries.open_question: Should the system track or integrate with passenger compensation workflows?

discoveries.title: On-board ticket purchasing or fare management
discoveries.discovery: The stakeholder interview touches on passenger management and alternative transport arrangements, but does not explicitly detail ticket purchasing functions.
discoveries.source_basis: Mention of ticket acceptance on other routes and alternative travel options.

discoveries.title: Indoor station navigation
discoveries.discovery: Station staff manage passenger flow and communicate platform changes, but specialized indoor navigation for passengers was not discussed.
discoveries.source_basis: Platform changes and station staff responsibilities in guiding passengers.

discoveries.title: Advanced passenger seat reservations
discoveries.discovery: Short-forming, journey terminations, and cancellations impact passenger seating, but seat reservations are not part of the network controller's core toolset.
discoveries.source_basis: Short-forming and train cancellations affecting passenger capacity.

discoveries.title: Emergency Services
discoveries.discovery: Emergency services (police, fire, ambulance) take command of life safety aspects during unexpected journey terminations and major incidents.
discoveries.source_basis: Mentioned under unexpected journey terminations and operational incidents as taking command of life safety.
discoveries.open_question: What level of direct system access or communication interface do emergency services require?

discoveries.title: Infrastructure Engineers
discoveries.discovery: Infrastructure teams are responsible for carrying out repairs, assessing track/signal safety, and accessing the track following incidents.
discoveries.source_basis: Mentioned in operational incidents and unexpected journey terminations regarding repairs and track access.
discoveries.open_question: How will engineering teams log onto the system to request and release track access authority?

discoveries.title: Real-time Network Map display
discoveries.discovery: The system needs to provide a visual display of all active trains, schedules, actual positions, speeds, and signal indications.
discoveries.source_basis: Listed under general information and tools for a network controller.

discoveries.title: Incident Management System
discoveries.discovery: The controller uses an incident management system to log, track, and manage all operational disruptions.
discoveries.source_basis: Listed under general tools as the Incident Management System.

discoveries.title: Communication systems integration
discoveries.discovery: Direct links are required to drivers (GSMR/radio), signallers, station managers, TOC control rooms, and emergency services.
discoveries.source_basis: Listed under communication systems in the controller's general tools.
discoveries.open_question: Which specific communication protocols (GSMR, radio, text, voice) must be integrated directly into the software interface?

discoveries.title: Performance monitoring and dashboards
discoveries.discovery: Dashboards showing network punctuality, delay attribution, and resource availability are necessary for strategic monitoring.
discoveries.source_basis: Listed under performance monitoring tools.

discoveries.title: Infrastructure and weather status monitoring
discoveries.discovery: The system must display real-time information on track conditions, signalling faults, power supply, engineering works, and live weather updates.
discoveries.source_basis: Described under infrastructure status and weather monitoring sections.

discoveries.title: Missing journey states during incidents
discoveries.discovery: Journey states such as 'Incident-affected - Stationary', 'Awaiting recovery', 'Passenger evacuation underway', and 'Line Blocked' need to be tracked.
discoveries.source_basis: Explicitly listed under missing journey states in section 7.

discoveries.title: Late notification of cancellation
discoveries.discovery: Late notification of cancellation can lead to passengers waiting unnecessarily at stations.
discoveries.source_basis: Identified explicitly under failure scenarios in the cancellations section.
discoveries.open_question: What automated alerts can reduce the window between a cancellation decision and passenger notification?

discoveries.title: Unclear authority during cancellations
discoveries.discovery: Unclear authority can lead to delays in decision-making and inefficient network use during service cancellations.
discoveries.source_basis: Mentioned under failure scenarios in the cancellations section.

discoveries.title: Station staff resistance to platform changes
discoveries.discovery: Station staff may resist platform changes due to accessibility challenges, overcrowding, or insufficient passenger notification time, posing safety concerns.
discoveries.source_basis: Described under conflicting responsibilities in the platform changes section.
discoveries.open_question: How should the system handle a veto or warning raised by station staff against a controller-initiated platform change?

discoveries.title: TOC service maintenance vs. Infrastructure safety
discoveries.discovery: Pressure from TOCs to maintain services can conflict with safety concerns from infrastructure engineers, requiring the controller to act as arbiter prioritizing safety.
discoveries.source_basis: Described under conflicting responsibilities in the operational incidents section.

discoveries.title: Passenger train diversions vs. Freight service priorities
discoveries.discovery: Diverting a critical passenger train might necessitate delaying or cancelling a vital freight service on the alternative route.
discoveries.source_basis: Described under conflicting responsibilities in the route changes section.
discoveries.open_question: Does the system provide automated decision support to weigh the priority trade-offs between passenger and freight services?

discoveries.title: Strict audit logging of all actions
discoveries.discovery: Every decision, instruction, and authorization must be logged with a precise timestamp and the identity of the authorizing individual.
discoveries.source_basis: Listed under key audit requirements across all scenarios.

discoveries.title: Communication and data archiving
discoveries.discovery: All voice and text communications, real-time train movement data, and infrastructure status data must be archived for later analysis.
discoveries.source_basis: Listed under communication records and real-time data archiving requirements.

discoveries.title: Reduced mobility passenger platform evaluation
discoveries.discovery: Alternative platforms must be checked for accessibility and specific needs for passengers with reduced mobility during platform changes.
discoveries.source_basis: Mentioned under information needed for platform changes.
discoveries.open_question: How will accessibility metadata for each platform be maintained and queried by the system?

discoveries.title: Passenger Information Systems integration
discoveries.discovery: Updated plans, diversions, cancellations, and platform changes must be communicated to Passenger Information Systems and station staff.
discoveries.source_basis: Mentioned across delay mitigation, platform changes, and route changes.

discoveries.title: Multi-party operational authorization flow
discoveries.discovery: Departures, running order adjustments, and emergency stops rely on a strict chain of authority involving the Network Controller, Signallers, Station Staff, Drivers, and TOCs.
discoveries.source_basis: Detailed throughout sections 1 through 8 regarding who provides information, makes decisions, and authorizes actions.

discoveries.title: Driver route competence verification
discoveries.discovery: It is assumed that the network controller or TOC can reliably verify whether an assigned driver is competent and familiar with a diversionary route before authorizing it.
discoveries.source_basis: Mentioned under route changes where driver familiarity with the route must be confirmed.
discoveries.open_question: Is driver route competence tracked automatically within the system or verified manually?

discoveries.title: Commercial vs Operational cancellation distinction
discoveries.discovery: Cancellations involve a commercial decision by TOCs based on resources and a separate operational cancellation by the Network Controller to free up paths, but the exact workflow boundary is fluid.
discoveries.source_basis: Described in the cancellations section regarding TOC commercial decisions versus network controller operational cancellations.
discoveries.open_question: Can an operational cancellation be triggered automatically if a TOC fails to confirm resource availability by a specific threshold time?
